set.typical_award_size: $200,000 per unit for category one (condos, townhomes, multifamily units and conversions of non-residential or non-code-compliant space; single-family homes are not eligible), $125,000 per ADU and $50,000 per SRO unit, paid at completion once the 55-year workforce Use Deed Restriction is recorded. Funding: $1,000,000 inaugural NOFA LP-001 (April 2025) reserved $725,000 for two Kings Beach projects (Steelhead Avenue Cottage Court, 3 tiny homes, $600,000; accessible ADU, $125,000). The February 2026 NOFA LP-002 offered $3,275,000 ($3,000,000 of new TOT approved February 3, 2026 plus $275,000 carryover), drew 12 applications ($10,550,000 requested) and reserved $3,250,000 for four projects: Lake Forest Multifamily (12 studios, Tahoe City, $2,400,000), Dollar Hill Tiny Homes (3 units, $600,000) and two tiny home ADUs ($125,000 each).
set.affordability_requirement: Units must be in unincorporated eastern Placer County within the Tahoe Truckee Unified School District boundary, outside avalanche hazard areas, with entitlements in place or allowed by right. A 55-year Use Deed Restriction (restarting on each transfer) requires occupancy as a primary residence by a qualified household with a local worker employed within the TTUSD area; no income limit or sales price cap. Units used to meet the Affordable Housing and Employee Accommodation Ordinance are ineligible.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The February 2026 NOFA (applications February 25 to March 18, 2026) is fully reserved. The County opened a community survey in August 2026 to guide guideline revisions that staff will bring to the Board; a future NOFA depends on new TOT funding recommended through the NTCA TOT-TBID Dollars at Work program.
set.cycle_notes: NOFA rounds when TOT funding is approved (April 2025, February 2026); 3-week application windows; randomized lottery prioritizing categories one and two when oversubscribed; projects have 2 years from reservation to reach certificate of occupancy. Guidelines under revision after the August 2026 survey.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (HUD PBV rule, Subpart D): for PBV development activity involving nine or more contract units, owners and contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages; existing housing and development with fewer than nine PBV units are not covered. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-24/subtitle-B/chapter-IX/part-983/subpart-D
